messages.content: Calculate the profit margin of a company with revenue of $200,000 and expenses of $150,000.

function.name: calculate_ROI
function.description: Calculate the Return on Investment (ROI) for a given investment amount and net profit. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

investment_amount.description: The initial amount of money invested. This is a float type value.

net_profit.description: The profit made from the investment. This is a float type value.

duration_years.description: The duration of the investment in years.

message.content:
Profit margin = \(\dfrac{\text{Revenue} - \text{Expenses}}{\text{Revenue}}\)

\[
\text{Profit} = \$200{,}000 - \$150{,}000 = \$50{,}000
\]

\[
\text{Profit margin} = \frac{\$50{,}000}{\$200{,}000} = 0.25 \; \text{or} \; 25\%
\]

So the company’s profit margin is **25 %**.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "Calculate the profit margin of a company with revenue of $200,000 and expenses of $150,000." Profit margin = (Revenue - Expenses) / Revenue. So profit = 200k - 150k = 50k. Profit margin = 50k / 200k = 0.25 or 25%. The user didn't ask for ROI. So no function call. Just answer.
